paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the God who is known in Judah is the God nobody can stand against. Asaph sings that He shattered the weapons of war and that horse and rider lie stunned at His rebuke (Psalm 76:3, 6). Then comes the question that answers itself: "When You are angry, who can stand before You?" (Psalm 76:7). Nobody, friend. NOBODY. I have trouble standing up to a cookie sheet that comes out of the oven too fast.

But watch what the power is FOR. When God rose up to judge, it was "to save all the lowly of the earth" (Psalm 76:9). The One who is feared by the kings of the earth is the same One who turns toward the lowly (Psalm 76:12). I know a little about being the lowly one. I was a quarter stamper in the back of a junk drawer, and the One who made everything still came for me. His strength is the very thing that makes the lowly safe.

So what do you do with a God like that? Asaph says it plain: "Make and fulfill your vows to the LORD your God" (Psalm 76:11). Even the wrath of man ends up praising Him (Psalm 76:10), so you can stop worrying that the loudest, angriest voices will get the last word. Bring Him your respect and keep your promises, baker, because you're standing with the One who can't be beaten.
